  *****NOTE FROM THE CITY*****

Doors to the City Council Chamber will open at 12:40 p.m. for Closed Session and 1:30 p.m. for Open
Session. Please be mindful, however, that there is limited seating in the City Council Chambers;
therefore, the Gladys Waddingham Lecture Hall (located adjacent to the Main Library) will be opened
as an overflow room and will be available for the public to watch the meeting and to speak.

ALTERNATIVE METHODS
The City provides the following two alternative methods of viewing and listening to the City Council Meeting as a
convenience:

  ¡  On Spectrum Cable Channel 35 with audio and limited video. Please check with your cable provider

  ¡  Live online through Facebook Live, with audio and limited video, at

The disruption in service of any alternative method does not preclude the City Council or other legislative body
from taking further action on an agenda item.

Submitting Comments Prior to Public Meeting: Members of the public may choose to submit comments
electronically for consideration by the City Council or other City Legislative Body by sending them to the City
Clerk/Secretary at athompson@cityofinglewood.org, and Deputy City Clerk at aallen@cityofinglewood.org. To
ensure distribution to the members of the Legislative Body prior to consideration of the agenda, please submit
comments prior to 8:00 a.m. the day of the meeting, and in the body of the email, please identify the agenda
number or subject matter. Correspondence should indicate the meeting date and agenda item. Comments received
after 8:00 a.m. and prior to the close of the public hearings will be made part of the official public record of the
meeting. Contact the Office of the City Clerk at 310-412-5280 with any questions.

minutes_text:
Inglewood, California
  April 18, 2023

The City Council of the City of Inglewood, California held a regular meeting on Tuesday,
April 18, 2023, in the Council Chambers in City Hall of said City.

Mayor Butts called the City Council into Closed Session at the hour of 1:00 p.m.

The Acting City Clerk announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present:  Mayor Butts, Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk;
  and
  Absent:  None.

City officials and personnel present for closed session were as follows:

  Angela Allen  Acting City Clerk
  Ken Campos  City Attorney
  Louis Atwell  Acting City Manager
  Christine Padilla  Staff Assistant

PUBLIC COMMENTS REGARDING CLOSED SESSION ITEMS. Mayor Butts
inquired if there were any persons present who wished to address the City Council on
Closed Session Item No. CS-1.

There was no response.

Mayor Butts recessed the City Council at the hour of 1:01 p.m. for Closed Session Item
No. CS-1.

  *****************

Following the Pledge of Allegiance to the flag of our Country, Mayor Butts called the City
Council into joint session with the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority at the hour
of 2:00 p.m.

The Acting City Clerk/Acting Successor Agency Secretary/ Acting Housing Authority
Secretary announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present: Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts,
  Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority
  Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, and Faulk; and
  Absent: None.

City/Successor Agency/Housing Authority officials and personnel present were as follows:

  Aisha L. Thompson  City Clerk/Secretary*
  Artie Fields  City Manager/ Executive Director*
  Ken Campos  City Attorney/General Counsel*
  Louis Atwell  Assistant City Manager/Public Works Director
  Christine Padilla  Acting City Clerk/Staff Assistant
  Destinee Wesley  Staff Assistant

* Serves as indicated for the Successor Agency, and Housing Authority.

PUBLIC COMMENTS – AGENDA ITEMS. Mayor/Successor Agency
Chairman/Housing Authority Chairman Butts inquired if there were any persons present
who wished to address the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority on any item
on the Agendas.

Speaker (Name Unknown) commented on a matter not on the Agenda, and was advised to
save his comment towards the end of the meeting to address his concern.

  1
   April 18, 2023

142.9  PAYMENT OF WARRANTS AND BILLS. It was moved by Council Member/
  Successor Agency Member / Housing Authority Member Morales, and seconded by
  Council Member/Successor Agency Member/Housing Authority Member Faulk that the
  demands presented to the City Council/Successor Agency/Housing Authority dated April
  13, 2023, in the amount of $6,393,752.65 are hereby allowed, and the City Clerk/Successor
  Agency Secretary/Housing Authority Secretary is hereby authorized to certify upon said
  registers that said demands are so approved. The motion was carried by the following roll
  call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members/Successor Agency Members/Housing Authority Members
  Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor/Successor Agency Chairman/Housing
  Authority Chairman Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  Council Member Gray pulled Agenda Item No. 5, to have a brief discussion.

132  CLAIMS DENIED. Letters from the Office of the City Attorney recommending the
  following:
  A. Reject Claims Pursuant to Government Code, Section 913:
  1. David Bullock for alleged property damage (tire); pothole on January 17, 2023.
  2. Katrina George for alleged property damage; fallen tree on January 1, 2023.
  3. Jerry Hawkins for alleged property damage; water pipe on January 16, 2023.
  4. Nicole Richard for alleged property damage (tire and wheel); pothole on December 24,
  2022.
  5. Rosalyn Rogers for alleged property damage; (tire) pothole on January 10, 2023.
  6. Richard Urrea for alleged tire damage; pothole on January 5, 2023.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby reject Claims listed as A-1 through A-6. The motion was
  carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

101  PAYMENT AUTHORIZED – COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES OF ANIMAL CARE
  & CONTROL (DACC). Staff report dated April 18, 2023, was presented recommending
  that the Mayor and Council Members authorize the immediate payment of the February
  2023 invoice submitted by the County of Los Angeles Department of Animal Care &
  Control (DACC) for housing and general animal care and control services provided to the
  City of Inglewood.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  the City Council does hereby authorize immediate payment in the amount of $55,735.91,
  payable on or before April 25, 2023. The motion was carried by the following roll call
  vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

  2
   April 18, 2023

101  RESOLUTION NO. 23-86 ADOPTED – ADOPTION OF THE UPDATED 2023
  LOCAL HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN (LHMP). Staff report dated April 18, 2023,
  was presented recommending that the Mayor and Council Members adopt a resolution
  adopting the 2023 Updated Local Hazard Mitigation Plan (LHMP).

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Faulk that
  Resolution No. 23-86 entitled:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA ADOPTING THE UPDATED LOCAL
  HAZARD MITIGATION PLAN AND AUTHORIZING SUBMITTAL OF
  THE PLAN TO THE CALIFORNIA GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF
  EMERGENCY SERVICES AND FEDERAL EMERGENCY
  MANAGEMENT AGENCY FOR APPROVAL

  be adopted. The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

301  SECOND AMENDMENT TO AGREEMENT NO. 21-147 APPROVED – THE
  ARROYO GROUP. Staff report dated April 18, 2023, was presented recommending that
  the Mayor and Council Members approve a Second Amendment to Agreement No. 21-147
  with The Arroyo Group, extending the term to December 31, 2024.

  Christopher Jackson, Economic and Community Development Department Director
  presented a brief overview.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby Approve Second Amendment to Agreement No. 21-147.
  The motion was carried by the following roll call vote:
  Ayes: Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes: None.

132.6  CLOSED SESSION – CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEY/CLIENT PRIVILEGED;
  WORKERS COMPENSATION CLAIM OF JOSE FERNANDEZ: CLAIM NO. 20-
  146150. Closed Session – Confidential – Attorney/Client Privileged; City Council
  Conference with Legal Counsel – Anticipated Litigation pursuant to Government Code
  Section 54956.9(d)(2); Worker’s Compensation Claim of Jose Fernandez: Claim Number
  20-146150.

  It was moved by Council Member Morales, and seconded by Council Member Padilla that
  the City Council does hereby approve the request for settlement. The motion was carried by
  the following roll call vote:
  Ayes:  Council Members Gray, Padilla, Morales, Faulk, and Mayor Butts; and
  Noes:  None.

126  REPORTS – ACTING CITY CLERK. The Acting City Clerk, Christine Padilla,
  reported that the City Clerk attended the blood drive at SoFi Stadium, which was a lovely
  event. She also reported that April was Autism Acceptance Month.

  PUBLIC REMARKS. Mayor Butts inquired if there were any persons present who
  wished to address the City Council on any matter connected with City business not
  elsewhere considered on the Agenda.

  Speaker (Name Unknown) welcomed and congratulated Council Member Gloria Gray. She
  stated that she looked forward to seeing her on the Council. She also stated that she hoped
  Council Member Gray would be a voice that speaks on behalf of the people and advocates
  for what the community wants. Additionally, she mentioned the closure of schools within
  the Inglewood Unified School District and requested the support of the Council.

  3
 April 18, 2023

  Emmanuel Lupe, Director of Public Relations for the International We Love You
  Foundation, Southwestern Region, thanked Mayor Butts and Council Members Padilla
and Faulk for their attendance and support at the blood drive. He also thanked the rest of the
Council Members for their hospitality. He said the International We Love You  Foundation
mega blood drive was historic. It was the single largest blood drive in the history of Los Angeles
County. Emmanuel reported that 1,135 blood donations were  collected from donors all over
California, including Arizona and Nevada, to join their  life-saving efforts. He also reported
that their partners at Cedar Sinai Livestreams  confirmed that the blood would save over
3,400 lives in local hospitals and medical centers throughout Los Angeles County, including
the City of Inglewood. Finally, he added that blood donations had decreased nationwide, and
the donations collected on  Sunday were valuable.

  Council Member Gray left the dais at the hour of 2:28 p.m.

  Council Member Gray returned to the dais at the hour of 2:30 p.m.

  There being no further business to be presented, Mayor Butts declared the meeting
adjourned in the memory of Curtis Rogers, Donna Allison, Lenny Smith, and Ryan Times
  at the hour of 2:32 p.m.

  Approved this 1st day of August, 2023.

  _____________________________
  Christine Padilla, Acting City Clerk

  ________________________
  James Butts, Jr., Mayor
